headings.title: Definition of levy as actual seizure of property
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'levy' for chapter 513 as the actual seizure of property by the officer charged with executing the writ.

headings.title: Definition of real estate including manufactured homes
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'real estate' for chapter 513 to include lands, tenements, hereditaments, and qualifying manufactured homes under sections 700.010 and 442.015(7).

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, statutory history, and effective date 3-01-11; definitions of 'levy' and 'real estate' (including qualifying manufactured homes under sections 700.010 and 442.015) verified.

headings.title: Preferred status for laborer wages up to one hundred dollars
headings.reviewNote: Grants preferred-creditor status up to one hundred dollars per employee for laborer or servant wages earned within six months before seizure, suspension, or receivership, paid pro rata after costs if insufficient.

headings.title: Statement under oath, payment priority, and claim contest procedure
headings.reviewNote: Requires sworn wage statement within ten days of seizure or thirty days of receivership/trusteeship, directs payment from sale proceeds after costs, and allows verified contest requiring judgment.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and statutory history; tightened subsection 1 title while preserving the $100 six-month wage preference and subsection 2 sworn-claim/contest procedures.

headings.title: Third-party claim of property, creditor indemnification bond, and levy release
headings.reviewNote: Requires officer to deliver third-party verified property claim to execution creditor and abandon levy unless creditor provides an approved indemnification bond within a reasonable time.

headings.title: Claimant forthcoming bond for possession and return of property
headings.reviewNote: Permits claimant, if creditor gives bond, to take possession before sale by delivering an approved forthcoming bond to preserve property, produce it as directed, and pay adjudged costs.

headings.title: Suit on bonds for breach by injured persons
headings.reviewNote: Permits any injured person to sue on such bonds in the name of the state for breach of condition and recover sustained damages if the execution creditor gave bond.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections and statutory history; corrected a critical mismatch in subsection 3, which authorizes injured persons to sue on the bonds for breach rather than governing surety objections.

headings.title: Return of claim and bonds to court and docketing
headings.reviewNote: Requires officer to return third-party claim and bonds on or before first day of next term, with clerk docketing and trial at that term unless continued for cause.

headings.title: Creditor response deadlines and civil practice rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires execution creditor to answer or move by second day of term, permits claimant reply as directed, and applies civil pleading and practice rules as far as practicable.

headings.title: Release order and judgment for costs upon creditor default or claimant judgment
headings.reviewNote: Directs court to order property release and enter judgment for costs against execution creditor and sureties upon creditor failure to respond or judgment for claimant.

headings.title: Special execution and sale order upon judgment for execution creditor
headings.reviewNote: Directs judgment against claimant and sureties and an order of sale operating as a special execution when judgment is for the execution creditor.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections and statutory history; officer return and docketing, creditor second-day response rule, release/costs on default or claimant win, and special execution sale order verified.

headings.title: Real estate execution sales at Hannibal courthouse in Marion County
headings.reviewNote: Requires execution sales of Marion County real estate in Mason and Miller townships under Marion County district 2 or other court-of-record judgments to occur at the Hannibal courthouse door.

headings.title: Real estate execution sales at Cape Girardeau courthouse
headings.reviewNote: Requires execution sales of Cape Girardeau County real estate under Cape Girardeau circuit court process at Cape Girardeau to occur at the Cape Girardeau courthouse door.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, statutory history, and effective date 1-02-79; Hannibal courthouse door location for Marion County Mason/Miller townships and Cape Girardeau courthouse door location verified.

headings.title: Debtor examination order within five years of unsatisfied return
headings.reviewNote: Pre-2027 version permitting judgment creditor within five years of an unsatisfied execution return to obtain an examination order for debtor or corporate chief officer, enforceable by attachment and contempt.

headings.title: Discretionary grant of use immunity by prosecutor
headings.reviewNote: Pre-2027 version permitting prosecuting or circuit attorney to grant use immunity from prosecution for statements made at a subsection 1 debtor examination.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, Revisor's dual-version note (2026 H.B. 1870 / S.B. 835 & 1111 delayed effective date), and 2012 Nothum v. Walsh annotation; distinguished pre-2027 five-year unsatisfied-return and discretionary prosecutor use-immunity version from 1-01-27 version 513.380:60207.

headings.title: Debtor examination order before satisfaction or presumed payment
headings.reviewNote: Effective 1-01-27 version entitling judgment creditor upon motion before satisfaction of record and before section 516.350 presumed payment to an examination order for debtor or corporate chief officer, enforceable by attachment and contempt.

headings.title: Statutory use and derivative use immunity for examination statements
headings.reviewNote: Effective 1-01-27 version granting statutory full use and derivative use immunity coextensive with constitutional self-incrimination privilege for examination testimony, except for perjury or false statement.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, effective date 1-01-27 (A.L. 2026 H.B. 1870 merged with S.B. 835 & 1111), and 2012 Nothum v. Walsh annotation; distinguished 1-01-27 motion-before-satisfaction/section 516.350 and statutory full use/derivative use immunity version from 513.380:27713.

headings.title: Triennial Consumer Price Index adjustment of statutory exemption amounts
headings.reviewNote: Mandates triennial CPI-U adjustment (rounded to nearest twenty-five dollars) of section 513.430 and 513.475 exemption amounts beginning April 1, 2029.

headings.title: Publication of adjusted exemption schedule by revisor of statutes
headings.reviewNote: Directs revisor of statutes by March 1, 2029 and every three years thereafter to publish adjusted amounts annually in an RSMo appendix with revisor's notes (includes original-rolls footnote on 'amounts*').

headings.title: Inapplicability of adjustments to cases commenced prior to adjustment date
headings.reviewNote: Provides that subsection 1 adjustments do not apply to cases commenced before the adjustment date.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections, effective date 1-01-27 (L. 2026 H.B. 1870 merged with S.B. 835 & 1111), and original-rolls footnote ('amount' in S.B. 835 & 1111); triennial CPI-U adjustments starting April 1, 2029, revisor publication, and prior-case exclusion verified.

headings.title: Exempt personal property and benefits from attachment and execution
headings.reviewNote: Pre-2027 schedule exempting listed personal property, insurance, public/disability/retirement benefits, wrongful death payments, firearms, and education savings accounts from attachment and execution.

headings.title: Exception for child support and maintenance orders against retirement assets
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that this section does not exempt IRC Sections 408 and 408A retirement plan assets from valid judicial or administrative child support or maintenance orders.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections (including subdivisions (1)-(13)), Revisor's dual-version note, and 1992 In re Vickers annotation; distinguished pre-2027 exemption schedule ($3,000 household goods/vehicles, $500 jewelry, $600 wildcard, $5,000 mobile home) from 1-01-27 version 513.430:60209.

headings.title: Exempt personal property, vehicle allocation, and health savings accounts
headings.reviewNote: Effective 1-01-27 schedule with raised dollar caps, up to $10,000 unused household exemption allocation to motor vehicles, and IRC Section 223 health savings account exemption.

headings.title: Exception for child support and maintenance orders against retirement assets
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that this section does not exempt IRC Sections 408 and 408A retirement plan assets from valid judicial or administrative child support or maintenance orders.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections (including subdivisions (1)-(13)), effective date 1-01-27 (A.L. 2026 H.B. 1870 merged with S.B. 835 & 1111), and 1992 In re Vickers annotation; distinguished 1-01-27 version raising household ($15,000), jewelry ($1,700), wildcard ($1,700), vehicle ($5,000 plus $10,000 unused household allocation), and mobile home ($12,000) caps and adding IRC Section 223 HSAs from 513.430:51255.

headings.title: Levying officer notice of execution and statutory exemption rights
headings.reviewNote: Requires levying officer within three days of levy to notify debtor by summons-manner service or regular mail of execution, sections 513.430 and 513.440 exemptions, and claim procedure.

headings.title: Verified exemption claim filing, creditor notice, and appraisal by householders
headings.reviewNote: Permits debtor to file verified exemption claim within twenty days, requires forthwith creditor notice except wage garnishments, and permits officer to summon three sworn disinterested householders to appraise property.

headings.title: Release of exempt property and expedited court review of exemption determinations
headings.reviewNote: Requires officer to release selected exempt items and permits aggrieved party to request expedited court review held within thirty days on at least three days' notice.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections, statutory history, and 3 case annotations (Union Reddi-Mix, Dancer v. Cheunault, Meeks Leasing); officer three-day notice, twenty-day verified claim and optional householder appraisal, and thirty-day expedited court review verified.

headings.title: Exemption from execution for county, municipal, and political subdivision property
headings.reviewNote: Defines covered political subdivision entities and exempts their courthouses, jails, clerks' offices, buildings, lots, burial grounds, and other lands from attachment and execution.

headings.title: Consent to mechanics' liens on public property leased for private use
headings.reviewNote: Permits covered public entities to record acknowledged written consent subjecting property leased primarily for private nongovernmental construction to chapter 429 mechanics' liens.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and 2025 H.B. 199 amendment; note catchline refers to county/municipal property while subsection 1 covers all listed political subdivisions, and subsection 2 permits recorded consent to chapter 429 mechanics' liens.

headings.title: Homestead exemption from attachment and execution up to fifteen thousand dollars
headings.reviewNote: Pre-2027 version exempting homestead dwelling, appurtenances, land, and rents/products up to fifteen thousand dollars, with aggregate cap across multiple claiming owners.

headings.title: Spousal alienation restrictions and requirement of joint conveyance
headings.reviewNote: Declares separate spousal sale, mortgage, or alienation of homestead null and void while preserving joint conveyance or disposition by husband and wife.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, Revisor's dual-version note, and section 442.025 cross-reference; distinguished pre-2027 $15,000 homestead exemption from 1-01-27 $40,000 version 513.475:60210.

headings.title: Homestead exemption from attachment and execution up to forty thousand dollars
headings.reviewNote: Effective 1-01-27 version exempting homestead dwelling, appurtenances, land, and rents/products up to forty thousand dollars in aggregate value, with aggregate cap across multiple claiming owners.

headings.title: Spousal alienation restrictions and requirement of joint conveyance
headings.reviewNote: Declares separate spousal sale, mortgage, or alienation of homestead null and void while preserving joint conveyance or disposition by husband and wife.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, effective date 1-01-27 (A.L. 2026 H.B. 1870 merged with S.B. 835 & 1111), and section 442.025 cross-reference; distinguished 1-01-27 $40,000 aggregate homestead exemption from 513.475:27731.

headings.title: Civil forfeiture of property used in or derived from criminal activity
headings.reviewNote: Subjects property used or intended for use in, derived from, or realized through criminal activity to civil forfeiture via a CAFA forfeiture proceeding.

headings.title: Application of rules of civil procedure to CAFA proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Governs CAFA forfeiture proceedings under Missouri rules of civil procedure except where special procedural rules are stated.

headings.title: Disposition of seized property dependent upon CAFA forfeiture outcome
headings.reviewNote: Bars disposition of seized property under section 542.301 or sections 447.500 to 447.595 unless the CAFA proceeding does not result in forfeiture.

headings.title: In rem CAFA forfeiture petitions for abandoned or unclaimed property
headings.reviewNote: Permits prosecutor or attorney general to institute an in rem CAFA forfeiture proceeding for abandoned or unclaimed property before or after seizure.

headings.title: In personam CAFA forfeiture actions before or after seizure
headings.reviewNote: Permits prosecutor or attorney general to bring an in personam forfeiture action before or after seizure in lieu of or in addition to an in rem proceeding.

headings.title: Pre-seizure writs, warrantless seizures, reporting, and filing deadlines
headings.reviewNote: Governs pre-seizure petitions and ex parte writs of seizure, warrantless seizures incident to lawful arrest/search/inspection, four-day reporting, ten-day petition filing, and agency burden of proof.

headings.title: Service of petition and notice of seizure upon interested parties
headings.reviewNote: Requires service of petition and seizure notice on all known interested persons under civil rules and permits service by publication for unknown or unlocatable parties.

headings.title: Annual seizure reports to public safety director and state auditor
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual January 31 open-record seizure reports from prosecutors and attorney general to the director of the Department of Public Safety with a copy to the state auditor.

headings.title: State auditor annual compilation report to general assembly
headings.reviewNote: Requires state auditor to compile seizure data and submit an annual report for the previous calendar year to the general assembly by February 28.

headings.title: Penalty for intentional or knowing reporting noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Classifies intentional or knowing noncompliance with section reporting requirements as a class A misdemeanor punishable by a fine up to one thousand dollars.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 10 subsections, statutory history, and 2 case annotations (Douthit, Karpierz); fixed subsection 8 omission of Department of Public Safety director recipient and refined subsections 5, 6, and 10 to match exact statutory text.

headings.title: Intervention by interested claimants and possession upon posting bond
headings.reviewNote: Permits any claimant to intervene before judgment and entitles claimant upon motion and value bond to take possession without removing property from court jurisdiction absent court order.

headings.title: Court-ordered sale of property by innocent secured parties upon default
headings.reviewNote: Permits court to order sale of property by an innocent lienholder or secured party when the underlying obligation is in default, with excess proceeds paid into court.

headings.title: Interlocutory judicial orders regarding property pending final judgment
headings.reviewNote: Permits court pending final forfeiture judgment to make any other state-law disposition of property in the interest of justice.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections, statutory history, and effective date 3-17-86; claimant intervention and bonded possession, innocent lienholder default sale, and interlocutory court dispositions verified.

headings.title: Stay of CAFA proceeding pending criminal disposition and innocent owner protection
headings.reviewNote: Mandates stay of CAFA proceeding pending related criminal charges, requires felony guilt for forfeiture, bars forfeiture without charges, and protects innocent owners under sections 513.610 to 513.620.

headings.title: Stay and release on bond absent felony conviction or guilty plea
headings.reviewNote: Mandates stay and release of seized property on value-capped bond and court conditions when no felony conviction, finding of guilt, or guilty plea supports forfeiture.

headings.title: Judicial approval of settlements and prohibition on plea bargaining with seized property
headings.reviewNote: Requires express court approval of CAFA settlements, bars using seized property in plea/sentencing bargaining, and prohibits accepting payments for release of property or criminal settlement.

headings.title: Time limits on holding seized property and judicial extensions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits holding seized property without timely section 513.607 petition unless circuit court grants filing extensions up to ten days per order and thirty days total.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections and statutory history; mandatory stay during criminal charges, felony guilt requirement, innocent-owner priority, bonded release, court settlement approval, plea-bargaining ban, and filing-extension caps verified.

headings.title: Relation back of state title to CAFA lien notice, lis pendens, or seizure
headings.reviewNote: Establishes relation back of state forfeiture title to CAFA lien notice, section 527.260 lis pendens, or final judgment recording for real property/beneficial interests, and to seizure date for personal property.

headings.title: Action for value and costs upon disposition of property after notice or petition
headings.reviewNote: Permits investigative agency to sue in circuit court for fair market value, investigative costs, and attorney's fees when property is disposed of after CAFA lien notice or petition.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, statutory history, and effective date 3-17-86; relation-back dates for real property (CAFA lien notice, lis pendens, or judgment recording) and personal property (seizure), and value/costs recovery action verified.

headings.title: Recognition and enforcement of reciprocal foreign forfeiture judgments
headings.reviewNote: Provides reciprocal recognition and enforcement in Missouri courts for valid forfeiture judgments from jurisdictions with laws substantially similar to sections 513.600 to 513.645.

headings.title: Attorney general authority to execute reciprocal forfeiture agreements
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes attorney general to enter into reciprocal agreements with attorneys general or chief prosecutors of jurisdictions with substantially similar forfeiture laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, statutory history, and effective date 3-17-86; reciprocal enforcement of foreign forfeiture judgments and attorney general reciprocal-agreement authority verified.

headings.title: Filing and recording of CAFA lien notice in county land records
headings.reviewNote: Permits investigative agency upon civil forfeiture suit or criminal indictment/information to file a CAFA lien notice in county official records without filing fee.

headings.title: Required contents and execution of CAFA lien notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires CAFA lien notice to be signed by attorney general, prosecutor, or designee and list five specified items (includes S.B. 450 'this act*' footnote).

headings.title: Limitation of CAFA lien notice to single person and related entities
headings.reviewNote: Limits each CAFA lien notice to one person plus aliases and controlled entities, requiring separate notices for other persons.

headings.title: Transmission of notice copy to named person
headings.reviewNote: Requires investigative agency to furnish a copy of the notice to the named person as soon as practicable, with failure not invalidating the notice.

headings.title: Attachment of state lien to real property and beneficial interests
headings.reviewNote: Creates a state lien upon filing against then-owned or after-acquired real property and beneficial interests of the named person in the filing county.

headings.title: Duration and priority of CAFA lien over subsequent interests
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the CAFA lien attaches at filing, continues until expiration, termination, or release, and takes priority over subsequently acquired interests.

headings.title: Filing of lis pendens and joinder of subsequent interest holders
headings.reviewNote: Permits investigative agency in a civil proceeding to file a lis pendens without court order and join subsequent interest holders as defendants.

headings.title: Trustee disclosure duties upon actual knowledge of CAFA lien notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires a trustee with actual knowledge of a CAFA lien notice or proceeding to disclose beneficiary details and trust instrument immediately, with noncompliance a class C misdemeanor.

headings.title: Trustee financial liability for conveying title after CAFA lien notice
headings.reviewNote: Imposes financial liability on a trustee who knowingly conveys real property subject to a CAFA lien notice, measured by the greater of proceeds or fair market value, capped if proceeds are held.

headings.title: No lien on trustee record title and civil enforcement actions against trustee
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that a CAFA lien notice is not a lien on trustee record title unless trustee is named, and permits civil recovery of subsection 9 amounts, investigative costs, and attorney's fees.

headings.title: Named person's property use and rent retention before forfeiture
headings.reviewNote: Preserves the named person's right to use property and receive rents or avails from use and ownership (but not sale) until forfeiture judgment is entered.

headings.title: Exceptions for court-ordered, recorded-trust, and beneficiary conveyances
headings.reviewNote: Exempts court-ordered trustee conveyances (except trustee-beneficiary actions) and, absent actual knowledge, conveyances under public-record trust agreements or to all beneficial owners.

headings.title: Protection of innocent person rights in forfeitures and dispositions
headings.reviewNote: Requires all forfeitures and dispositions under this section to make due provision for the rights of innocent persons.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 13 subsections, effective date 3-17-86, and S.B. 450 'this act' footnote; refined subsections 11 and 12 to avoid unstated 'Debtor' and inaccurate 'public trusts' wording.

headings.title: Six-month pre-judgment term and six-year post-judgment renewal periods
headings.reviewNote: Sets CAFA lien notice term at six months pre-judgment (one renewal) and six years post-judgment (one renewal).

headings.title: Authority of investigative agency to release CAFA lien notice without fees
headings.reviewNote: Permits investigative agency to execute full or partial CAFA lien notice releases for recording in county official records without fee.

headings.title: Termination of CAFA lien notice upon criminal acquittal or dismissal
headings.reviewNote: Terminates CAFA lien notice with no effect upon criminal acquittal or dismissal if no civil forfeiture proceeding has been instituted.

headings.title: Expedited judicial action to release or extinguish CAFA lien notice
headings.reviewNote: Permits named person when no civil proceeding is pending to sue for release or extinguishment with five-to-ten-day hearing, pending-sale escrow release, or security posting (includes 'this act*' footnote).

headings.title: Relief available during pendency of civil CAFA proceeding
headings.reviewNote: Permits court, upon motion of a named person while a civil proceeding is pending, to grant the release relief provided in this section.

headings.title: Dismissal of civil CAFA action upon criminal acquittal or dismissal
headings.reviewNote: Mandates dismissal of a civil CAFA action upon acquittal or dismissal of a criminal action against a person named in the CAFA action.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 6 subsections, effective date 3-17-86, and S.B. 450 'this act' footnote; pre- and post-judgment terms/renewals, fee-free agency releases, criminal-acquittal termination/dismissal, and expedited release actions verified.

headings.title: Restrictions on transferring seized property to federal agencies
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits state or local agencies from transferring seized property to federal agencies without review and approval by both prosecuting attorney and circuit judge, multistate activity or written U.S. attorney intent to prosecute, and a felony violation.

headings.title: Statement filing, property owner notice, challenge petition, and hearing
headings.reviewNote: Requires ex parte prosecutor statement, court certification and mailed owner notice, ninety-six-hour owner challenge petition to delay transfer, and ten-day evidentiary hearing.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, statutory history, and 2 case annotations (State v. Sledd, Karpierz v. Easley); verified prosecutor-and-judge approval requirement, felony/multistate/federal-intent criteria, and 96-hour owner challenge procedure.

headings.title: Annual report of federal forfeiture seizures and proceeds to state auditor
headings.reviewNote: Requires law enforcement agencies using the federal forfeiture system to file an annual report with the state auditor by February 15 consisting of the federal ACA Equitable Sharing Agreement and Certification form.

headings.title: Funding ineligibility penalty for noncompliance with federal reporting
headings.reviewNote: Renders any law enforcement agency that intentionally or knowingly fails to comply with section reporting ineligible for state or federal law enforcement, safety, or criminal justice funds.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and statutory history; annual February 15 state auditor reporting using the federal ACA Equitable Sharing form and funding-ineligibility penalty for intentional or knowing noncompliance verified.
